note: Netarsudil was taken to patients on IOP lowering in normotensive monkeys and rabbits; ATS907 and DE-104 failed Phase 2 with no public model data.
label: Glaucoma ROCK

engagement.note: One drop of netarsudil 0.04% raised tonographic outflow facility 53% and cut aqueous flow 20% in normotensive monkeys.
engagement.quote: Six hours after a single dose of 0.04% AR-13324 to 7 normal monkey eyes, C was increased (P<0.05) by 53% in drug-treated eyes compared with either contralateral vehicle-treated control eyes or baseline measurements.
engagement.judgement: Opens at 2012: FDA's pharmacology review says the primary pharmacology was reviewed under the initial IND review filed 3-7-2012; the paper itself printed 2015 (no online date in Crossref).

engagement.note: In healthy volunteers netarsudil 0.02% raised outflow facility 22% versus 53% in monkeys; aqueous flow fell only as a trend.
engagement.quote: In netarsudil-treated eyes, diurnal outflow facility increased from 0.27 ± 0.10 μL/min/mmHg to 0.33 ± 0.11 μL/min/mmHg (+22%; P = 0.02) after 7 days of treatment.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Sit 2021 (doi 10.1016/j.ajo.2021.01.019) repeated the outflow-facility rise in 20 POAG/OHT patients; it changes no status.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Kazemi does not set the monkey data beside the human data in the abstract. Outflow facility is physiology downstream of ROCK, so readout_tier downstream. 53% vs 22% is 2.4-fold; the monkey's second mechanism (aqueous flow -20%) only trended in humans (-15%, P=0.08), hence partial.
engagement.magnitude_basis: % increase in tonographic outflow facility (monkey 0.04% single dose vs human 0.02% 7 days)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Filed with the NDA as study AR-13324-APH08 (FDA PharmR 2017).
engagement.note: Netarsudil 0.04% cut episcleral venous pressure 35% and IOP 39% in Dutch Belted rabbits, measured by servonull micropipette.
engagement.quote: Three hours after AR-13324 dosing, IOP was reduced by 39%±7% (P<0.001) and EVP decreased by 35%±4% (P<0.05); after vehicle dosing, IOP was reduced by 24%±4% (P<0.05) and EVP increased by 25%±5% (P<0.05).
engagement.judgement: Opens at the paper's online date (2015-03); the human aqueous-dynamics study NCT02406287 started 2015-04, so the prediction was prospective.
engagement.model: Dutch Belted rabbit, invasive episcleral venous pressure, topical netarsudil 0.04%

engagement.magnitude_basis: % fall in episcleral venous pressure (rabbit 0.04% day 3 vs human 0.02% day 8)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Kazemi: 'Diurnal EVP was not significantly different between netarsudil- and placebo-treated eyes.' Sit 2021 (doi 10.1016/j.ajo.2021.01.019; NCT03233308, results 2019-06-11) found a significant -0.89 mmHg treatment difference in POAG/OHT patients; changes no status. FDA ClinPharmR (2017-08-28) states EVP reduction was shown 'in animal and human studies'.
engagement.note: EVP fell 10% in netarsudil-treated healthy-volunteer eyes versus 35% in rabbits; not significant against the vehicle eye.
engagement.quote: Diurnal episcleral venous pressure (EVP) in netarsudil-treated eyes decreased from 7.9 ± 1.2 mmHg to 7.2 ± 1.8 (-10%; P = 0.01).
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Kazemi does not cite the rabbit data in the abstract. Within-eye fall significant, between-eye difference not, hence partial. 35% vs 10% is 3.5-fold.
engagement.model: Dutch Belted rabbit, invasive episcleral venous pressure, topical netarsudil 0.04%

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Filed with the NDA as study AR-13324-IPH05 (FDA PharmR 2017); FDA ClinPharmR cites 'perfused human eyes' as mechanism evidence.
engagement.note: Netarsudil's active metabolite raised outflow facility 51% over baseline in perfused human donor eyes and dilated episcleral veins.
engagement.quote: Perfusion with netarsudil-M1 significantly increased C when compared to baseline (51%, P < 0.01) and to paired controls (102%, P < 0.01), as well as significantly increased PEFL in both IW (P < 0.05) and ESVs (P < 0.01).
engagement.judgement: Human tissue but not a dosed person, so a model (ex_vivo). Published 2016-11, before human outflow-facility data were public (NCT02406287 completed 2016-04, no posted results, published 2018), so prospective as far as public record shows.
engagement.model: Perfused enucleated human donor eyes, netarsudil-M1 0.3 μM

engagement.magnitude_basis: % increase in outflow facility over baseline (ex-vivo 3 h perfusion vs human tonography day 8)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Sit 2021 (POAG/OHT patients) repeated the rise; Kim 2024 (doi 10.1016/j.xops.2024.100533) found episcleral vessel diameter up ~27% in patients, matching the ex-vivo ESV dilation. Neither changes the status.
engagement.note: Outflow facility rose 22% in dosed healthy volunteers versus 51% in perfused donor eyes; same direction, smaller.
engagement.quote: In netarsudil-treated eyes, diurnal outflow facility increased from 0.27 ± 0.10 μL/min/mmHg to 0.33 ± 0.11 μL/min/mmHg (+22%; P = 0.02) after 7 days of treatment.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me. Ex-vivo dosing was the active metabolite at a fixed perfusate concentration, so the dose link is loose; 51% vs 22% is 2.3-fold. Kept to engagement: the system made no IOP or dose prediction for patients.
engagement.model: Perfused enucleated human donor eyes, netarsudil-M1 0.3 μM

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); facility magnitude not in abstract. Not among the NDA pharmacology studies.
engagement.note: Topical netarsudil widened trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal on OCT, raised outflow facility and lowered IOP in living mice.
engagement.quote: These changes occurred in conjunction with increased outflow facility, increased speckle variance intensity of outflow vessels, increased tracer deposition in conventional outflow tissues and decreased intraocular pressure.
engagement.judgement: Opens at the online date (2016-04). Sponsor co-authored mechanism study, run after the Phase 3 IOP results but before human outflow data, so not a retrodiction for engagement.
engagement.model: Living mouse eye, OCT of conventional outflow tissue, topical netarsudil

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both sides; mouse facility magnitude unknown, so direction only.
engagement.note: Outflow facility rose 22% in dosed healthy volunteers, the direction the mouse showed; no human OCT of Schlemm's canal was found.
engagement.quote: In netarsudil-treated eyes, diurnal outflow facility increased from 0.27 ± 0.10 μL/min/mmHg to 0.33 ± 0.11 μL/min/mmHg (+22%; P = 0.02) after 7 days of treatment.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me. Only the facility readout has a human counterpart; the OCT canal readouts were never measured in dosed patients that I found.
engagement.model: Living mouse eye, OCT of conventional outflow tissue, topical netarsudil

dose.note: Monkey and rabbit pharmacology used netarsudil 0.04% once daily as the effective concentration.
dose.quote: The IOP measured by pneumatonometer in treated eyes was reduced (P<0.005) by 25% when compared with baseline measurements and by 24% when compared with contralateral vehicle-treated eyes.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at the IND year (2012), per the FDA pharmacology review.

dose.note: Patients reached an effective concentration: 0.02% once daily, half the monkey's 0.04%, cut IOP 5.7 mmHg; 0.04% also worked but was less tolerated.
dose.quote: On day 28, mean diurnal IOP was 20.1, 20.0, and 18.7 mmHg in the AR-13324 0.01%, 0.02%, and latanoprost groups, respectively, representing a decrease from unmedicated baseline of 5.5, 5.7, and 6.8 mmHg (P<0.001).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The 7-day dose-ranging study CS201 (0.01/0.02/0.04%) is known only from the FDA clinical pharmacology review: '0.02% had similar efficacy but superior tolerability compared to netarsudil 0.04%'.
dose.judgement: Paired by me; year 2015 is the print date of the monkey paper (the trial epub is 2014-09). Topical drug with no measurable plasma level, so concentration is the only dose metric. No margin_stated: the corneal-haze NOEL margin was 1, so the model did not state that the effective concentration was free of that finding; the corneal harm is scored in safety.
dose.magnitude_basis: topical concentration giving IOP reduction (model 0.04% vs human 0.02%)

efficacy.note: Netarsudil lowered IOP ~25% in normotensive monkeys and gave large, 24-h IOP reductions in Dutch Belted rabbits.
efficacy.quote: AR-13324 reduces IOP in normotensive monkey eyes.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the IND year (2012). Normotensive animals, not a glaucoma model: the system relied on was IOP lowering in healthy eyes.

efficacy.note: Netarsudil lowered mean diurnal IOP 5.7 mmHg (~22%) in glaucoma/OHT patients, as the monkey (~25%) predicted; it missed non-inferiority to latanoprost.
efficacy.quote: On day 28, mean diurnal IOP was 20.1, 20.0, and 18.7 mmHg in the AR-13324 0.01%, 0.02%, and latanoprost groups, respectively, representing a decrease from unmedicated baseline of 5.5, 5.7, and 6.8 mmHg (P<0.001).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. ATS907 and DE-104 failed Phase 2 per a review (Wang & Chang 2014, doi 10.2147/OPTH.S41000) only; no primary source or model data found, so neither is scored.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. The model predicted IOP lowering, not a margin against an active comparator; the IOP endpoint responded in every netarsudil trial, so 'same' although Phase 2b and ROCKET-1 missed non-inferiority (ROCKET-1 met it only post hoc at baseline <25 mmHg). ~22% = 5.7 of ~25.7 mmHg baseline, back-calculated from the abstract.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: % IOP reduction from baseline (monkey 25% vs patients ~22%)
efficacy.reason: IOP fell in patients as predicted

patient_trials.quote: Study 301 failed in its primary endpoint and netarsudil was not non-inferior to timolol in patients with baseline IOP < 27 mmHg.
Study 302 achieved success in its primary endpoint and demonstrated that netarsudil was non-inferior to timolol in patients with a baseline IOP < 25 mmHg.

efficacy.confidence_note: Opening date from the cited GWAS (Verma 2024, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2023.12.006, PMID 38242088, taken from the reference list; not read).
efficacy.note: African-ancestry GWAS (Verma 2024, Cell) mapped a POAG risk allele to ARHGEF12, a RhoA activator upstream of ROCK.
efficacy.quote: Variants within the Rho/ROCK signaling pathway, including loci at ARHGEF12 and ROCK1P1, were identified based on prior genome-wide association analyses
efficacy.judgement: Opens at the GWAS year, when the genotype became available as a candidate patient selector for ROCK inhibitors.
efficacy.model: ARHGEF12 rs11824032 risk genotype (African-ancestry POAG GWAS) as predictor of netarsudil response

efficacy.magnitude_basis: difference in ≥20% IOP-reduction rate by genotype
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text (PMC13194400). Retrospective EHR cohort, n=66 (114 eyes), most on concurrent medications; aOR 1.31 (95% CI 0.42-4.10). The hypothesis was undirected ('may influence response').
efficacy.note: In 66 netarsudil-treated POAG patients, ARHGEF12 carriers and non-carriers reached ≥20% IOP reduction at similar rates (35% vs 30%).
efficacy.quote: ARHGEF12 variant carriers did not show a statistically significant difference in treatment response assessed by IOP; however, given the small sample size, particularly among homozygous carriers, and concurrent use of multiple glaucoma medications, these findings should be interpreted cautiously
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison: the paper tests the genotype's prediction against patient IOP response. Scored contra because the source says the genotype 'does not strongly predict' response; low confidence because the null is underpowered and exploratory. Netarsudil was already approved, but the patient-level answer was not known, so not a retrodiction.
efficacy.model: ARHGEF12 rs11824032 risk genotype (African-ancestry POAG GWAS) as predictor of netarsudil response

safety.note: Rabbit and monkey topical toxicology showed dose-dependent conjunctival hyperemia and, in monkeys, corneal haze; NOEL margin for haze was 1.
safety.quote: The NOEL for corneal haze provides an exposure margin of 1 at the intended clinical dose.
safety.judgement: Opening at the IND year (2012), when the first ocular toxicology was reviewed. The quote comes from the 2017 review.

safety.note: Patients showed the harms the animals did: conjunctival hyperemia (50-53%) and corneal verticillata (5-26%), which FDA linked to the monkey corneal haze.
safety.quote: As noted by the applicant, it is possible that the finding of corneal haze in monkeys is related to the findings of “corneal deposits” and “corneal verticillata” associated with Netarsudil Ophthalmic Solution 0.02% treatment
safety.confidence_note: The regulator calls the haze-verticillata link 'possible'; FDA notes the monkey haze arose and resolved faster than the human deposits. Lin 2017 (doi 10.1089/jop.2017.0023, epub 2017-06) had already reported mild hyperemia as the only animal adverse effect.
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by the reviewer. Year 2017: Lin 2017 (June) paired with Bacharach 2014 already showed the hyperemia match; the review is dated with the December 2017 approval (public posting date not checked). Magnitude direction_only: the model called hyperemia mild and transient, while it was the leading patient AE.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence of conjunctival hyperemia and corneal deposits
safety.reason: Hyperemia and corneal deposits both predicted
